summary: The candidate is a substantive partial implementation: it adds a shared RouterGate and neutral bf16-to-fp32 helper, migrates the issue's specifically named precision-fix models plus the six prior-review counterexamples, preserves fp32 router outputs in the tested paths, and passes its focused tests. It does not satisfy the original repository-wide consolidation contract. Twenty model files still explicitly instantiate ReplicatedLinear for a gate/router, two additional model-local MoE gate classes remain outside RouterGate, and a representative untouched bf16 ReplicatedLinear returns bf16 logits. Independently, deterministic mode is not batch invariant on the assigned MI355X at a realistic 4096x128 router shape: the same token differs between batch sizes 1 and 8 by 3.62396240234375e-05, contradicting the shared layer's stated batch-invariant policy even though top-k did not flip in this sample.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: the shared sglang.srt.layers.moe.router_gate module does not exist on the recorded base.
Candidate regression suite: 5 tests passed, covering CPU fp32 output/reference, fp32 mode, correction-bias naming, deterministic tiny-dispatch bypass, and the legacy helper alias.

Independent MI355X GPU boundary cases M=1,8,9,16,17,32,64,65 returned fp32 with max absolute error 4.58e-05 to 8.20e-05 versus a CPU fp32 reference. A representative untouched bf16 ReplicatedLinear returned bf16. One hundred two-stream trials did not reproduce scratch corruption.

For one identical bf16 token and weight [128,4096], deterministic mode produced non-identical fp32 logits at M=1 and M=8 (max absolute delta 3.62396240234375e-05); top-8 indices remained equal for this sample.

tests.command: source audit: rg -l 'self\.(gate|router) = ReplicatedLinear\(' python/sglang/srt/models/*.py plus local nn.Module gate scan (on candidate)
tests.what_was_measured: Found 20 model files with explicit ReplicatedLinear gate/router construction and local Glm4MoeLiteGate and XllmMoEGate classes outside RouterGate.
All changed candidate Python sources compiled successfully.

tests.command: prepared-interpreter import audit for 14 migrated model modules
tests.what_was_measured: Imports resolved to /job/repo/python on the exact candidate checkout for Bailing variants, DeepSeek-v2, Kimi Linear, LLaDA2, GLM4-MoE, Hunyuan-v3, Laguna, Mimo-v2, MiniMax-M3, Nemotron-H, Sarvam-MoE, and Step3.5.

gpu_execution.evidence: Executed on one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx95, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2); raw outputs are under reports/j-4b77e59ded70/raw/.

remaining_counterexamples: Deterministic RouterGate output is not batch invariant on MI355X for hidden size 4096 and 128 experts: the same token differs by 3.62396240234375e-05 between M=1 and M=8.

Twenty model files still explicitly construct a ReplicatedLinear gate/router, including Mixtral, Qwen2/3 MoE, Llama4, Grok, DeepSeek, and other MoE families; these bypass RouterGate's output-dtype and dispatch policy.
Glm4MoeLiteGate and XllmMoEGate remain model-local nn.Module gate implementations rather than RouterGate consumers.
A representative bf16 ReplicatedLinear used by remaining consumers returns bf16 logits, so the proposed every-model fp32-router-logit contract is false.
remaining_limitations: No model weights were available, so full checkpoint loading, serving, semantic accuracy, accumulated long-CoT effects, and end-to-end performance were not tested.
The assigned device was AMD Instinct MI355X. NVIDIA CUDA tiny-GEMM, HPC-Ops, DeepGEMM, Intel AMX, NPU, XPU, distributed, and non-gfx95 paths remain unverified.
No native source changed in the candidate, repository-environment.json declares native=null, and imports resolved to candidate Python sources; therefore no native rebuild was applicable.
The concurrent-stream scratch test did not reproduce corruption in 100 trials; this does not prove safety on other scheduling patterns or architectures.
